diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: A citizen in a video addressed the officials of the Islamic Republic, demanding their resignation. He said they have destroyed the youth of the people. He also stated that death is better than living under their rule.
A citizen in Azna was arrested in connection with the December 1404 protests. The arrest was carried out by the Intelligence Forces of the IRGC. Further details have not been released.

Ali Farhadi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Education, denied the issuance of plaques for students. He warned that school principals should not raise issues that cause concern among families. The Ministry of Education described this action as playing with the students' mental peace.

Hamrah Aval and Irancell have increased their call, SMS, and internet package tariffs by up to 40 percent. These changes have been implemented since the early hours of Friday, the first of Aban. The tariff increase also includes fixed internet services such as TD-LTE and fiber optic (FTTx).

Hadi Jalali, a teacher and political prisoner in Jiroft prison, has gone on a hunger strike protesting his detention conditions and lack of access to his medications. This action was taken due to his poor detention conditions. Hadi Jalali is a resident of Kerman.

Donald Trump accused LeBron James of disrespecting America by doing practice moves during the national anthem. Trump posted a video on Truth Social, called James a 'disgrace' and demanded an apology. James responded by saying it was probably a slow news day.

Typhoon Champi has reached Taiwan with heavy rains and strong winds. One person has died and 94 have been injured, with about 1300 people evacuated. Activities in Taiwan have stopped and there is still a chance of the typhoon making direct landfall.
Farshad Rezaei, a citizen from Divandareh, was released on Wednesday, October 21, after posting bail from a security detention center in Sanandaj.
A video shows a long line of cars waiting for gasoline at a fuel station in Mashhad. The video was recorded on Thursday evening. The report was published by Iran International.

Hossein Aghaei from Iran International says the potential war between the US, Israel, and the Islamic Republic is at stage zero. The first 72 hours could determine the outcome of the conflict. Israel is likely to target officials and infrastructure to keep the war short.

The Asian Football Confederation announced its support for Gianni Infantino's re-election as FIFA president after previously criticizing him. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa praised Infantino at the Tokyo congress and pledged full support. This support came after disputes over FIFA's financial plan and Infantino's apology.

Abdollah Hajisadeghi stated that Mojtaba Khamenei manages the country's affairs despite wartime conditions and limited public presence. He said the leader manages the revolution, the three branches of government, and the armed forces with health and firmness. He also emphasized that the confrontation with Israel will continue until the resistance's goals are achieved.

The Tabriz Civil Registration Office issued a birth certificate for a child named 'Sayghi' 70 days after birth. Previously, issuance was refused due to the absence of the Turkish name 'Sayghi' in the system. After the parents' complaint and review in Tehran, the child's name was registered.

Reports from the public indicate internet outages and slowdowns in various Iranian cities amid increased military and security presence. Citizens from Mashhad, Astara, and Tehran have reported increased government forces and communication restrictions. These reports were published by Iran International.

The French government has put about 80,000 police officers on alert. Gatherings in Lyon, Marseille, and some urban centers have been banned. Labor unions, students, and Yellow Vest activists are preparing for widespread protests.

The head of the Social Emergency Center of the Welfare Organization announced that last year about 9,000 working and street children received daily services and 3,000 others received round-the-clock services. He reported the lack of accurate statistics on waste-picking children and warned about the transfer of working children to underground workshops.

Amir Hatami, the commander of the Islamic Republic's army, announced that the country is expanding its drone production centers. He also stated that they have adequate reserves. These remarks were made at the underground drone production center.

Ali Shirazi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the justification by Islamic Republic officials for not releasing the image, voice, and handwriting of Mojtaba Khamenei contradicts his claimed leadership and authority. He questioned which institutions decide on Mojtaba Khamenei's presence and interaction with society. These remarks point to restrictions on Mojtaba Khamenei's public presence.

A citizen in Kerman stated that the absence of free fuel cards has made obtaining gasoline difficult. He said that after the vehicle card quota is used up, getting gasoline becomes problematic. This issue was raised in a message to Iran International.

Ata Hosseinian stated that the 10,000 toman gasoline plan has been implemented in five provinces of Iran. Emergency fuel cards at gas stations have been collected. The Islamic Republic is considering increasing gasoline prices and limiting its consumption.

A poll by the Times of Israel shows that both the pro-Netanyahu and opposition blocs have 51 seats each, falling short of the 61-seat majority. The Yesh Atid party leads with 23 seats, followed by Likud with 21 seats. These results complicate the formation of the government.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei responded to Donald Trump's threat about using the 'mother of bombs' by warning that Iran's armed forces will use the 'father of missiles' against US positions. He called Trump's threats a bluff and said the Iranian people are ready to confront them. These remarks were made in an interview with IRNA.

Eyal Zamir, Chief of Staff of the Israeli Army, stated that Israeli forces prevented a major terrorist operation during a clash with two armed individuals in the West Bank on Friday. Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the siege of Hebron and a complete blockade of entry and exit to the West Bank. A widespread wave of arrests against Hamas terrorists has also begun.

Reuters, citing American researchers, reported that satellite images indicate the development of a ballistic missile production factory in Saudi Arabia's Al-Dawadmi. The factory is likely being prepared to produce larger solid-fuel missiles with longer range. The factory is expected to be ready for production by the end of this year.

Ebrahim Salimi, nursing director of Ilam University of Medical Sciences, reported a shortage of staff in the university's medical centers. To reach the national standard for nurse-to-bed ratio, hiring 682 nursing staff is essential. Additionally, about 180 more assistant nurses are needed.

Itamar Ben-Gvir called for the dissolution of the Palestinian Authority and restrictions on Palestinian movement in the West Bank. Two Palestinians were killed and several injured in a shooting near Hebron. The Israeli army killed two suspects and continues its search operation.

Sasan Ghandehari, an Iranian-born billionaire, previously had a business partnership with Astan Quds Razavi. Between 2013 and 2016, he was the main investor in a fiber optic network project in Iran. This project was carried out in cooperation with Astan Quds Razavi.

The price of Mobile Internet has increased by about 40% since November 1. Users complain about reduced internet package volumes and poor internet quality. Additionally, in cities like Dezful, Tehran, and Astara, the security atmosphere has intensified with the presence of military forces and installation of security cameras.

Reza Pahlavi wrote in an article in Le Figaro asking French presidential candidates to make four specific commitments to support the Iranian people, condemn the suppression of protesters, ensure free internet access, and protect Iranians abroad. He identified the Islamic Republic as responsible for the attack on French forces in Beirut and a threat to Iran and the West. The article was published on the 43rd anniversary of the attack on the Drakkar building.

New information from citizen accounts to Iran International reveals that during the December protests in Sistan and Baluchestan, IRGC agents tortured detained women in front of their families. This issue was discussed by Farzad Fattahi in the program "Geography of the National Revolution."

The deputy technical and executive officer of Tehran Municipality announced the implementation of a plan to collect child laborers and deal with flower sellers in the Behesht Zahra area and Hashemi Highway. These actions were carried out in cooperation with the Traffic Police, Social Services Organization, and Welfare Organization. After the plan's implementation, the presence of flower sellers blocking the highway routes has significantly decreased.

Hossein Simaei-Sarraf, Iran's Minister of Science, invited veiled girls from Azerbaijan to continue their studies at Iranian universities in a video message. There is no nationwide hijab restriction in Azerbaijani universities. Reports have emerged of veiled students being barred from some schools.

One month after the school year began, the problems of Om Kolthoom girls' school in Iranshahr remain unresolved. The unsafe building and lack of educational facilities endanger the students' lives. Students are studying without desks, chairs, or shelter in the heat of Baluchestan.

A shooting in the Yvelines area west of Paris resulted in one death and several injuries. Police have arrested a suspect, but the motive remains unclear. The French anti-terrorism prosecutor's office is investigating the case.

Politicians and experts in the Danish parliament discussed the future of Iran and the impact of the Islamic Republic's activities on European security. A representative of the Danish People's Party warned about the security threats posed by the Islamic Republic. He called for a free and democratic Iran.

Armed unknown individuals attacked a church in Karak province, Jordan, on Friday, killing and injuring several people. The attack occurred during a funeral ceremony. Security forces are pursuing the suspects, and no further details have been released.

The prosecutor of Dezful announced that women riding motorcycles in the city will be dealt with. An order has been issued to confiscate their vehicles and file legal cases against women motorcyclists. This restriction is related to the non-issuance of motorcycle licenses for women.

The president of the Japan Football Federation expressed doubts about holding the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia due to escalating Houthi attacks. The tournament is scheduled from January 7 to February 5. Saudi officials have stated that their top priority is the safety of players and fans.

Mohsen Hajimirzaei stated that the country's imports have decreased by 25% following the siege of southern ports. Previously, 75% of imports were conducted through these ports. Alternative trade routes have been activated using the capacity of 15 neighboring countries.

Maryam Rahmati, a journalist at Iran International in the UN headquarters, won the bronze award of the United Nations Correspondents Association in 2026. The award was given in the Ricardo Ortega Memorial category. The award ceremony will be held in December 2026 at the UN headquarters.

Following floods in the counties of Salmas and Maku, at least three people, including a ten-year-old girl, have died. Twenty-four residential homes have been flooded. Search and rescue operations are ongoing.

Brent oil prices on Friday, 1st of Aban, exceeded $114, reaching the highest level in five months. This price increase is attributed to tensions in the Middle East and reports of a possible US and Israeli attack on Iran. Additionally, natural gas prices in Europe rose by four percent on the same day.

Tehran officials have warned that if the US attacks again, attacks on Gulf countries will expand to include economic infrastructure and civilian targets. The threats include attacks on airports and oil pipelines. The Islamic Republic has stated it will target US forces more intensely.

Fars News Agency reported that the movement of unauthorized vessels in the Strait of Hormuz has been completely stopped. This followed the destruction of navigation aid systems and incidents involving several oil tankers. The IRGC warned that if oil smuggling resumes, harsher actions will be taken.

At the birthday ceremony of Akbar Seyed Hosseini, attendees chanted slogans at his grave: "This fallen flower is a gift to the homeland." He was killed at the age of 29 during the protests on January 9, 2026.

Kamran Farmanpour stated that the protection of 460,000 hectares of protected areas in Lorestan is the responsibility of 120 rangers. He identified staff shortages, funding issues, payment problems, building deterioration, and vehicle shortages as major environmental challenges in the province.

Hamas and Hezbollah issued separate statements declaring an armed operation at the northern entrance of Hebron as a response to Israeli attacks. Hamas stated that two people involved in the operation were killed in clashes with Israeli forces. Hezbollah described the operation as a legitimate response to Israeli crimes.
A sandstorm entered the Dashtiari area in Chabahar, Sistan and Baluchestan on Friday, the first of Aban. The storm covered the sky of the region. A video of these moments has been released.

Mostafa Sepahvand stated in a London court that the IRGC asked him to harm Kambiz Hosseini and Mojtaba Pourmohsen to stop their writing about the government. He claimed he accepted these requests out of fear and that his promises to carry out missions were to deceive the IRGC. The prosecution challenged this claim, saying Sepahvand is trying to justify his actions.

Alireza Kiani explained the difference between 'institution' and 'individuals' in the logic of Iranian monarchy on the program 16 'Fereydoun'. He stated that kings as individuals are measured by the respect they show to the monarchy as an institution. He also attributed the differing views of monarchists towards Shah Abbas and Shah Sultan Hossein to this logic.
The number of executions at Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad has increased to two. Another prisoner was executed in the early hours of Tuesday, October 20. This report was published by HRANA news agency.
A citizen criticized inflation and rising prices of consumer goods and food in a video sent to Iran International. He also protested the flag-waving by supporters of the government.

Laurent Nuñez, France's interior minister, announced that the shooting on Friday in the city of Trapp was a terrorist act. One person was killed and three were injured in the incident. The terrorism prosecution investigation is ongoing.

Lufthansa airline group announced the postponement of its planned resumption of flights to Dubai until the 4th of Azar. This decision was announced on the 1st of Aban without a stated reason for the delay. Previously, flights were scheduled to gradually resume from early Aban.

Jean-Yves Le Drian, the French foreign minister, said that escalating tensions between the Islamic Republic and the US has no winner and will harm all parties. He added that this tension could sharply increase oil and gas prices. These remarks were made after a meeting of foreign ministers from several countries in Istanbul.

Peter Kohlgraf, Archbishop of Mainz, took political sponsorship of Mahbubeh Shabani, a political prisoner sentenced to death, and called for her immediate release. This action was carried out with the follow-up of Behrouz Asadi, an Iranian human rights activist. Shabani was arrested on charges of helping injured protesters during the January protests.

Rouhollah Rahimpour referred to Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani's remarks about abandoning the fatwa banning nuclear weapons. He said some influential forces in the Islamic Republic want to build nuclear weapons. This action requires a fundamental change in the regime's military doctrine.

A video on social media shows that the birthday of Reza Rizvandi was held at his grave. Reza Rizvandi was killed at the age of 27 during the protests on January 9, 2026, in Pakdasht by government agents.

Businesses on Paris's Champs-Élysées covered their shop windows with wooden boards and metal barriers. This was due to concerns about violence and looting during planned protests. The French interior minister announced that 70,000 security forces will be deployed to maintain order.

Salman Es'haqi stated that the monthly cost of some foreign chemotherapy drugs for cancer patients exceeds 300 million tomans. The parliament estimated a shortage of nearly 800 drug items. It was also warned that the shortage of consumable equipment may lead to the closure of some operating rooms.

Majid Barzegar announced that two of his novels were banned despite having received publication permits. The novel "The Autumns That Will Come" was banned and its copies were ordered to be collected after the third printing. Additionally, permission to publish his second novel was not granted.

Johan Wadephul called for an end to attacks by the Islamic Republic and Houthis on shipping and neighboring countries. He emphasized that Tehran must be ready for a diplomatic solution and enter negotiations. Germany, Britain, and France are ready to play a role in nuclear talks.

Two suspects accused of planning a terrorist attack on a Jewish museum and a synagogue in Manchester appeared in London's Old Bailey court. Prosecutors stated that these individuals were in contact with a person in Iran and took orders from him. More details were reported by an Iran International journalist.

Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, stated that participants in the Istanbul meeting agreed on preventing the spread of war and emphasized the importance of diplomacy. They called for an immediate ceasefire in the Persian Gulf and Ukraine and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The meeting topics included the Ukraine war, Iran's situation, and maritime security.

The US Marine Corps conducts daily flights of stealth F-35C fighters from a base in the Middle East. These flights are part of their daily operations. The exact location of the base is not mentioned in the text.

Donald Trump said Washington can end the conflict with Iran very quickly and is deciding between ending the matter or waiting for the gradual weakening of the Islamic Republic. He also announced that the US Navy has blocked the Strait of Hormuz and denied reports of a two billion dollar payment to Jared Kushner. Trump added that the oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz last week was even higher than before the war.

Maryam Rahmati received the Ricardo Ortega Memorial Award for outstanding coverage of United Nations events. She reported on public protests, human rights violations, and the suppression of women in Iran and Afghanistan. The award will be presented in December 2026 in New York.

Mohammad Mokhber stated that the Islamic Republic knows the weaknesses of the opposing side and that field surprises and the leverage of oil and energy can disrupt the equations. He described the threats from Trump and Netanyahu as signs of desperation. Mokhber also emphasized that a nation that has lived in the region for thousands of years will remain.

The Turkish foreign minister stated that participants in the Istanbul meeting agreed on preventing the spread of war and emphasized the importance of diplomacy. The French foreign minister warned that escalating tensions between Iran and the US would have severe consequences for fuel prices. The meeting, initiated by Turkey, discussed regional security and shipping routes.

Scott Bessent stated that Washington has struck the main parts of Iran's oil export network in less than two months. He said the revenue sources of the IRGC have been severely limited and the shadow tanker fleet weakened. Bessent added that the US is ending the threat posed by the Islamic Republic.

Vincent Kompany, Bayern Munich's coach, was taken to the hospital by ambulance after experiencing a physical problem at the club's training center. He had been suffering from a severe viral infection and fainted during training. The exact details of his condition have not yet been officially announced.

Mike Waltz denied the statements attributed to him in the Financial Times report and called for a correction. He said the US Navy can continue the maritime blockade but did not comment on hypothetical scenarios. The decision on continuing the blockade and diplomacy is up to Donald Trump.

Alireza Nouri's mother mourned at his grave and vowed to take revenge, saying the blood will not remain on the ground. Alireza Nouri was killed by Islamic Republic agents during the protests on January 9, 2026, in Qazvin. This video was shared on social media.

Norway's Ministry of Foreign Affairs updated its official travel warning for Iran, urging its citizens to avoid traveling there. The ministry described the security situation in Iran and the region as tense and unpredictable. It also advised those currently in Iran to leave the country as soon as possible.

Babak Es'haqi, a reporter from Iran International, interviewed Sami Abu Shehadeh, the leader of the Balad party from the Joint Arab List. The interview took place ahead of the Israeli parliamentary elections.

Families of political prisoners executed in 1988 were prevented from entering Khavaran cemetery today and left their flowers behind closed gates. They held a ceremony at the site to honor the victims. The 1988 executions remain a significant political and human rights challenge in Iran.

In Mehr 1405, at least 79 prisoners, including two women, were executed in Iran. Additionally, 22 death sentences were issued and 11 were confirmed by the Supreme Court. Notable cases include the execution of Alisina Mostafavi and the reissuance of the death sentence for Varisheh Moradi.

On Friday, the first of Aban, the gates of Khavaran cemetery remained closed to the families of political prisoners executed in 1988. The families placed their flowers behind the closed gates and commemorated the victims with singing. In the summer of 1988, thousands of political prisoners were executed by order of Ruhollah Khomeini and buried in mass graves.

The head of the European Union delegation to the United Nations stated that the Iranian government should never acquire nuclear weapons and expressed concern over Tehran's lack of cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency. He called for strengthening the agency's safeguards system and supporting its technical and independent activities. He also warned about nuclear security risks in Ukraine and North Korea's weapons programs.

Two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran has plans to attack submarine communication cables in the Persian Gulf if the US and Israel attack again. The goal is to prevent cable repairs and cause prolonged communication disruptions. The location and method of the attacks were not disclosed.
A worker in Paveh County, Kermanshah Province, fell from a tree while harvesting walnuts and died. The incident occurred due to lack of workplace safety. The worker's death happened yesterday.

Al Nassr football team achieved their fourth consecutive win in the Saudi league by defeating Al Faisaly in the eleventh week. Cristiano Ronaldo scored in this match, bringing his professional career goals to 982. Abdullah Al-Hamdan also scored his third goal of the season.

France and the UAE have resumed talks to develop an upgraded version of the Rafale fighter jet after a pause earlier this year. Abu Dhabi's financial participation could reduce the pressure on France's defense budget. The UAE is likely to condition its involvement on receiving technology or partial production transfer.
The first 48 hours of the war are very important. Israel has a plan to increase its forces within the regime. This was reported by Iran International.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh criticized his players' performance after Esteghlal's 1-1 draw against Chadormalu Ardakan. He said the team played better in the second half and restored balance with substitutions. Bakhtiarizadeh also mentioned player fatigue but emphasized that Esteghlal should not play poorly even for one half.

Environmental reports in Iran last week highlighted air pollution, drying wetlands, and threats to wildlife habitats. The air quality index reached 500 in Masjed Soleyman and Abadan, and over one-third of the Choghakhor wetland dried up. Cases of illegal hunting, natural area fires, and waste management issues were also reported.

The foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt, and Pakistan called for the swift and complete resumption of safe and unobstructed passage through the Strait of Hormuz. They stated that the conflict between the US and Israel with Iran should be resolved only through dialogue and diplomacy. They also rejected any restrictions disrupting legal shipping.

Donald Trump said he has no knowledge about a possible attack on Iran. Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey, had previously confirmed the possibility of an attack on Iran over the weekend. Barrack also stated that the immediate nuclear threat from Iran has almost been resolved.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, has called on governments and organizations to submit documentation of human rights violations from September 2026 onward. Her next report will focus on issues such as cross-border repression of opponents, threats to families, women's rights, and the consequences of detention and execution. These documents will be submitted to the Human Rights Council for the report preparation.

Lionel Messi and Patti Smith received the Princess of Asturias Award on Friday, 22 October. The award ceremony was held in Oviedo, Spain, hosted by the Princess of Asturias. Messi dedicated this honor to his recently deceased father.

The 186th issue of the Peace Line magazine was published focusing on kolbari and fuel carrying in border areas. This issue examines the legal, economic, and social aspects of the phenomenon and its consequences. It includes interviews with officials and experts about security policies and the rights of border residents.

Donald Trump stated that another operation similar to 'Epic Fury' against the Islamic Republic might take place. He said if Tehran is wise, it will start serious negotiations, but he doubts this will happen. Trump criticized the Obama-era nuclear deal as one of the worst and predicted that oil prices will soon drop sharply.

Johan Wadephul, Germany's foreign minister, announced that Germany, along with France and Britain, is ready to negotiate with the Islamic Republic of Iran to prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons. These statements were made after a meeting of eight European and regional countries in Istanbul. Wadephul emphasized that Tehran must show serious readiness for a diplomatic and sustainable solution.

Donald Trump said Washington can end the war with the Islamic Republic very quickly. He mentioned the possibility of carrying out operations similar to 'Epic Fury.' Trump emphasized that Tehran can prevent another US attack by reaching an agreement.

Esteghlal football team drew 1-1 against Chadormalu Ardakan in the tenth week of the Premier League. It seemed that Esteghlal players were more tired than ever. Mozdek Mirzaei discussed this issue in the Hattrick program.

Mohammad Taghavi stated in the Hattrick program that Esteghlal had a weak defense in the match against Chadormalu. He noted that in previous games this season, Esteghlal's defense was strong. The Chadormalu team, coached by Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, criticized Esteghlal's defensive performance in this match.

As European diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions with the Islamic Republic continue, Benjamin Netanyahu's harsh remarks and US military movements have brought the possibility of a new round of conflicts into focus. Kambiz Tavana, a member of the Iran International editorial board, said the path of diplomacy and readiness for military action are proceeding in parallel. According to him, Donald Trump wants Tehran to accept specific conditions, and with the upcoming elections in the US and Israel, political and military calculations have become more complex.

Residents of Bandar Kong and Bandar Lengeh reported sounds of explosions and gunfire. A loud explosion and house shaking were heard in Bandar Kong. Similar sounds causing house vibrations were reported in Bandar Lengeh.

Behnam Taleblu, senior director of the Iran program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said the Islamic Republic's ability to build nuclear weapons depends on the fate of enriched uranium reserves after the 2025 attacks. According to him, if Tehran has hidden reserves, it is technically possible to advance the weapons program, although he personally does not believe such reserves exist.

The Esteghlal football team, despite a decent performance this season, faces issues such as a closed transfer window and the termination of Yaser Asani's contract. Additionally, a cooperation agreement with the National Sports Academy of Serbia has been signed. These topics were discussed in an interview between Mazdak Mirzaei and Raha Pourbakhsh.

Jaber Rajabi analyzed recent military developments in the Gulf countries as prompting a review of defense policies. He mentioned the possibility of Saudi Arabia moving closer to the US and Israel and the formation of new alliances. He also warned that in case of a new war, attacks by groups affiliated with the Islamic Republic from Iraq may increase.

The Israeli army announced a military operation in the Hebron area following the killing of two soldiers in an armed attack, which will last several days. The army forces are searching for weapons and interrogating suspects. Residents of the operation areas can leave through three designated routes after security inspections.

Hamid Alidousti, former national team player and current technical manager of Chadormalu team, has been ill for some time. He is one of Iran's well-known footballers. This issue was discussed in an interview with Mohammad Taghavi.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, announced that oil exports from the Persian Gulf have surpassed pre-conflict levels. He emphasized that Iran's threats have not stopped the flow of energy to global markets. Oil exports in the region are increasing strongly.

Leila Morvati said European countries seek a deal similar to the JCPOA with Iran, but Trump demands the complete end of Tehran's nuclear program. She added that the Istanbul meeting was ineffective due to the absence of main parties and lack of a clear roadmap. Morvati believes current mediation efforts to prevent renewed military conflict have a bleak outlook.

A vehicle carrying rebar lost control in Azimieh neighborhood of Karaj and its fuel tank exploded and caught fire after hitting a curb. The incident occurred on the evening of Friday, Aban 1. No report on the extent of damage has been released yet.

The Israeli parliamentary elections will be held on the 27th of October. These elections could lead to the continuation of Benjamin Netanyahu's premiership or the formation of a new government. Netanyahu needs the support of the parliamentary majority to form a government.

The Yemeni government army announced that in the past 24 hours, it carried out 1,392 attacks against Houthi positions as part of Operation Fajr Yemen. The army spokesperson said about 620 Houthi forces have left the battlefield and nearly 190 military vehicles and equipment were destroyed or damaged. Government forces advanced in the Al-Qurouj front in Taiz province, but these figures have not been independently verified.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iraq and Pakistan are restricting Iran's access to land trade routes by closing some border crossings. This intensifies the economic pressure from the US naval blockade and airline sanctions. According to the newspaper, the new restrictions deepen Iran's economic isolation.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, has called on governments and organizations to submit documents on human rights violations in Iran from September 2026 onwards. Her upcoming report will focus on cross-border repression of opponents, threats to families, and women's rights. The deadline for submitting information is November 15, 2026.

According to reports from University of Tehran students, security officers' confrontations with students, especially female students, have intensified at the start of the new academic year. Officers have increased pressure through threats, humiliation, confiscation of student cards, and preventing some students from entering. There are also reports of physical confrontation with a student at the entrance of 16 Azar Street.

The US Director of National Intelligence warned in a memo about significant progress in Iran's plans to assassinate American officials and citizens in the Middle East and some other regions. He proposed lowering the classification level of these documents to inform more at-risk personnel. Concurrently, the US State Department ordered a reduction of diplomatic staff and the departure of families and non-essential employees from embassies and consulates in several regional countries.

The US State Department announced it is reducing staff at its embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar, and the UAE due to concerns over escalating attacks by Iran-backed Houthis. This decision does not mean an evacuation order and the embassies remain open. These embassies were previously in limited operations status.

Donald Trump mentioned the possibility of an operation similar to 'Epic Fury' against the Islamic Republic. He said Tehran could prevent another attack through an agreement. Trump expressed doubt that Iranian officials would start serious negotiations.

Shayan Samiei does not rule out the possibility of an attack on the Islamic Republic before the US midterm elections or Israeli elections. The Islamic Republic is trying to show military superiority by displaying power and claiming to have laid mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The US is also sending a clear message of readiness for military confrontation by strengthening its forces and military equipment in the region.

Kambiz Tavana from Iran International said that US warnings about the Islamic Republic's plans to attack American citizens and personnel have increased. Meanwhile, European countries are trying to mediate and continue diplomacy. The naval blockade in southern Iran also continues, and pressure on Tehran remains.

Ali Mamouri, advisor to the former Iraqi prime minister, said restrictions on Iran’s trade routes and US pressure have challenged Baghdad to maintain balance in its regional relations. According to him, while Iraq depends on imports from Iran, it also strives to preserve ties with the US and other neighboring countries, as aligning with one side could have political and economic consequences for the country.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces, emphasized Iran's control over the Persian Gulf and the prohibition of American forces entering the area. He stated that the US should not expect its military to re-enter the Persian Gulf. These remarks were made in response to the possibility of renewed American attacks.

Masoud Pezeshkian traveled briefly to Mashhad on Friday evening and visited the burial site of Ali Khamenei and his deceased family members. No prior reports about this trip were published. No further details about the trip have been released.

In Mehr 1405, 66 deaths due to lack of safety at work and 288 cases of worker injuries were recorded. Additionally, 53 gatherings and 13 worker and union strikes were reported. These statistics reflect various violations of workers' rights.

A schoolgirl said in a video to Iran International that the heavy cost of school supplies has become difficult for her father to afford. She added that the Islamic Republic causes them to lose interest in studying and stop attending school.

Saeed Hasani, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Shiraz, has been held in Adelabad prison without a clear legal status for 124 days. No court session has been held to review his case so far. Authorities have not provided clear responses to his family's inquiries.

Mohammadreza Talebi, a Basij member injured during the December 1404 protests, died after about 9 months in a coma. He was injured on January 9 in District 7 of Tehran. This news was reported by the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said the Islamic Republic initially tries to buy time by showing readiness for negotiation and reduce the potential costs of war. He added that if this approach fails, Tehran may resort to military confrontation. The reason is that the cost of retreat is higher than continuing confrontation.
